q: What was the practice adopted by the Vijayanagar Kings to protect the inhabitants within a fortified area from starvation due to sieges by enemy armies?
options: Large granaries were built within the fortified area to store grains
Secret pathways were maintained to transport groceries into fortified areas
Large agricultural tracts were incorporated within the fortified area
The forts were built on hills to prevent siege by the enemy
key_text: Large agricultural tracts were incorporated within the fortified area
explanation: Vijayanagara enclosed large agricultural tracts within its fortifications so the city could feed itself during a siege - NCERT notes this was unlike the usual practice of building granaries.

notes.text: - **Against sieges:** Vijayanagara enclosed **large agricultural tracts within the fortified area** (APPSC G1 2017; NCERT Themes II ch. 7) – granaries were the usual practice elsewhere.

notes.text: - **Nuniz:** Portuguese (APPSC; NextGen PYQ book wrongly prints "Italy") – reign of **Achyuta Deva Raya**, not Krishnadevaraya, Sadasiva or Venkatapati II.

explanation: Krishnadevaraya brought the Balakrishna idol from Udayagiri fort (1513) and built the Balakrishna temple at Hampi to house it. Narasa Nayaka, Devaraya II and Tirumala Raya did not.

q: Hazara Ramaswamy temple was built by
explanation: The Hazara Rama temple at Hampi (Vijayanagara) was built by Sri Krishnadevaraya. Venkata (Aravidu), Sri Ranga and Lingama Nayaka are not its builders.

q: Which temple, renowned for its intricate carvings and temple complex consisting of three shrines dedicated to Lord Shiva, Lord Vishnu, and Lord Veerabhadra, is an example of Vijayanagara architecture?
explanation: The Lepakshi temple (Sri Sathya Sai, formerly Anantapur district) has three shrines - Shiva, Vishnu and Veerabhadra. Jagannath, Kedarnath, Somnath, Bugga Ramalingeswara and Chintala Venkataramana are elsewhere.

q: At which place was the Veerabhadreswara Swamy temple built by Penugonda Virupanna?
explanation: Penugonda Virupanna built the Veerabhadreswara Swamy temple at Lepakshi. Tadipatri, Hampi and Kadiri have other temples.

notes.text: - **Musical pillars:** **Vittala temple, Hampi** (UPSC 2007) – not Belur, Bhadrachalam or Srirangam.

q: Vijayanagara paintings were found here?
explanation: The Veerabhadra temple at Lepakshi has the finest Vijayanagara-school paintings in Andhra. Srisailam, Tirupati, Tadipatri, Simhachalam, Ahobilam, Pushpagiri, Draksharama and Vontimitta are known for other things.

q: During whose period did the officials (Virupanna and Veeranna) build the Lepakshi temple?
explanation: Virupanna and Veeranna built the Lepakshi temple c. 1530-40 under Achyuta Deva Raya. Krishnadevaraya died in 1529; Sadasiva and Venkatapati came later.

q: A famous huge stone Bull of the Vijayanagar period is located at
explanation: The huge monolithic Nandi of the Vijayanagara period is at Lepakshi. Tadipatri, Kadiri and Penugonda have no such bull.

q: Which kingdom is associated with the Lepakshi temple, famous for its mural paintings and hanging pillars?
